Analysis.description: The ``analysis`` block: statistics computed by the CLI, never recomputed here.
Analysis.title: Analysis

BudgetResult.description:
One policy budget's outcome within one scope.

``denominator`` is what separates "0/0, nothing was ever counted" from
"measured, and the answer is 0%". Both store ``observed = 0.0``, and both
clear a ceiling budget, so without it an unmeasured budget is indistinguish-
able from a clean one. See ``BUNDLE_SPEC.md`` for the field-by-field
contract and the compatibility rule for bundles that omit it.

conclusive.description: Whether `passed` is a conclusion rather than a coin flip. False when the budget had nothing to measure (an empty sample, or a quantity this run could not observe at all, such as a cost ratio where both models reported zero cost), or when a breach landed on too small a sample to separate `observed` from `allowed`. The interval test is asymmetric: only a breached budget is asked to defend itself (a ceiling breach needs `ci_low > allowed`, a floor breach `ci_high < allowed`), so a budget that held is conclusive whenever it was measured at all. An inconclusive budget is not a pass and not a failure: it is a check that did not reach a verdict, and consumers must not round it up to either. Defaults to true, which is also how a bundle that omits it is read.
conclusive.title: Conclusive

denominator.description: How many units `observed` was computed over — records for the rate budgets, tool-bearing records for tool drift, paired calls for the cost and latency ratios. 0 means the budget was evaluated against an empty sample, so `observed` is a default and not a measurement. Null means no sample size was reported, which is NOT the same as zero: bundles written before this field existed omit it, and consumers must treat its absence as 'unknown' and fall back to `conclusive`.
denominator.title: Denominator

Comparison.description:
One (prompt, evaluator-axis, slice) statistical verdict, as emitted by the CLI.

``kind`` is the evaluator's stable type slug, same as ``ExampleScore.kind``:
an evaluator measuring two axes emits one comparison per axis under the same
user-chosen name. Blank on bundles from CLIs predating the field.
Comparison.title: Comparison

Decision.description: The ``decision`` block: the migration verdict, mirroring the CLI ``MigrationDecision``.
Decision.title: Decision

Example.description:
One evaluated example, as emitted by the CLI.

Carries no per-example ``severity``: ``_classify_severity`` in the CLI
classifies a comparison *across* examples from a corrected p-value, Cohen's d
and n, and is undefined for a single row. Consumers rank on
``worst_delta_score`` instead.
Example.title: Example

ExampleScore.description:
One evaluator's paired verdict on one example, on one axis.

``kind`` is the evaluator's stable type slug (``tool_selection.divergence``),
as opposed to ``evaluator_name`` which is whatever the user called it in
``evalshift.yaml``. One evaluator can measure more than one axis — a
tool_selection evaluator with divergence on emits a conformance row and a
divergence row under the same name — so ``(evaluator_name, kind)`` is the
row's identity, not the name alone. Blank on bundles from CLIs predating
the field.
ExampleScore.title: ExampleScore

ExampleTrace.description:
What one model side actually did on one example.

``side`` admits ``"expected"`` so shipping golden-case events later needs no
migration; nothing emits it today.

Insights.description:
Machine-written narrative explaining the run.

Every headline figure on the page is rendered from data; this block is prose
only. The CLI validates that the generating model copied figures verbatim
from its facts block rather than deriving them.

The length caps are load-bearing: this text is model-generated, reaches a
rendered page, and must not be able to blow up a response or a table row.
